description: State government in collaboration with MyPerfectice launched an AI-based skill enhancement platform for IIIT Basara students

State government in collaboration with MyPerfectice launched an AI-based skill enhancement platform for IIIT Basara students
Hyderabad : The State government in collaboration with MyPerfectice startup, launched an AI-based skill enhancement platform for IIIT Basara students to address the challenges of engineering education. The startup is part of Telangana AI Mission (T-AIM) under its RevvUp programme. It is aimed at addressing the challenges of engineering education by providing personalized learning recommendations to students based on their knowledge gap and enhancing their cognitive and programming skills as per industry demand through coding practice and self-learning modules. With the help of technology and data insights, the platform empowers teachers and students to bring personalized learning to students. These courses are designed to develop the required proficiencies that align with industry requirements, ultimately enhancing student’s employability quotient. Telangana IT Principal Secretary Jayesh Ranjan said: “It is an excellent initiative that aligns with our vision of transforming the education system and creating a skilled workforce for the future. description: The Telangana AI Mission (T-AIM) launched the Mobility AI Grand Challenge to foster innovation for GHMC. In this challenge, GHMC aims to identify and classify pothole severity across specified routes in Hyderabad using live and archived video feeds.

The Telangana AI Mission (T-AIM) launched the Mobility AI Grand Challenge to foster innovation for GHMC. In this challenge, GHMC aims to identify and classify pothole severity across specified routes in Hyderabad using live and archived video feeds.
Hyderabad: The Telangana AI Mission (T-AIM) launched the Mobility AI Grand Challenge to foster innovation for GHMC. This is being taken up in partnership with Capgemini. The two concluded a similar challenge for the Forest Department earlier this month. In this challenge, GHMC aims to identify and classify pothole severity across specified routes in Hyderabad using live and archived video feeds. Through the solutions developed using artificial intelligence, GHMC officials will get additional insights to undertake targeted repair works in Hyderabad. Also Read Here are the speed limits for different roads in Hyderabad The challenge is open for applications. Innovators will be selected based on their approach note, and the shortlisted innovators will get four weeks to develop a Proof of Concept. The winning innovator will receive mentoring support and an award of up to Rs 20 lakh towards implementation of a potential pilot project with GHMC. “Governments and innovators should increasingly collaborate to solve social problems through open innovation. I am confident that this initiative of T-AIM will help GHMC use AI-based solutions to improve road safety,” said IT Principal Secretary Jayesh Ranjan. “We are using an open innovation ecosystem to select, advocate and support tech-enabled solutions to make a difference to people. Everyone can relate to pothole severity across India. The identification of viable solutions through the Mobility AI Grand Challenge will contribute to road safety,” said Anurag Pratap, VP and CSR Leader at Capgemini India. TiHAN, India’s first autonomous navigation facility at IIT Hyderabad, and INAI-IHub Data, the applied AI research centre at IIIT-H are partners in this challenge. While TiHAN will provide intellectual support, INAI-IHub Data will provide Bodhyaan 1.0, the data capture platform. The deadline to submit approach notes for the challenge is September 16. The winner will be announced in November.

Hyderabad: Telangana AI Mission (T-AIM) together with financial services company Wells Fargo launched the ‘Academic Grand Challenge’ to foster innovation in the banking sector. T-AIM is an initiative of the Government of Telangana, powered by Nasscom. In this challenge, student teams from India are expected to build solutions on two fronts. One involves building a futuristic, pure digital bank that integrates modern technologies to enable banking wherever and whenever. The other requires building a predictive analytics model to estimate financial markets performance during this year. The winning team will receive prize money and merchandise worth Rs 5 lakh. Registration details on taim-gc.in/academic . Teams will be selected based on their approach note and last date to send that is September 16. Shortlisted teams will get eight weeks to present a Proof of Concept. The submissions will be judged based on approach, technique and result. The winner will be announced in November. “It is encouraging to see the private industry encourage young talent through this initiative. Modern technologies, including artificial intelligence, have the ability to transform various sectors including banking,” said IT and Industries Principal Secretary Jayesh Ranjan. “Students are one of our best sources of original ideas. We hope that the Academic Grand Challenge will give students an opportunity to innovate solutions,” said Arindam Banerrji, EVP and Managing Director, Wells Fargo India and Philippines.

Hyderabad: Telangana AI Mission (T-AIM) started in May last year with the objective of facilitating AI startups to build their base in Hyderabad, works in critical areas identified by Telangana, enables government verticals to use AI solutions and works to contribute to the State’s GDP. Its CEO Snehanshu Mitra tells about the progress and plans to B Krishna Mohan of Telangana Today. Year of AI 2020 is considered as the year of artificial intelligence. The same year also witnessed pandemic but that did not stop us as we had busy 15 months so far. A lot of foundational effort has been put into it. Many industry collaborations have been forged so far and these actions have already started bearing fruits. Support The Telangana Government had an interaction with multiple startups. We are consolidating the solutions and promise that wherever there is an opportunity, the Telangana Government will be the first customer. An AI investment fund is on the cards. The corpus will be used for accelerating startup activities and the proposal is being shared with the Government, which is the approving authority. AI in agriculture Artificial intelligence for agricultural innovation is a priority for Telangana. We did a grand challenge for consolidation of use cases and data sets. We met with a good success in this. Two pilots are happening. While one pertains to real time price discovery and volume management at electronic marketplaces, the other use case is related to farmer lending using farm/output backed credit risk assessment. We will work with different agencies and partners including the Government wings like the forest department to look at use cases and develop proof of concepts for the State. title: AI adoption major focus for Telangana: Jayesh Ranjan
description: He highlighted that the AI framework unveiled under the IT policy focused on datasets, retrieving of data, skilling, infrastructure and setting standards of ethics in using data.
body_text:
He highlighted that the AI framework unveiled under the IT policy focused on datasets, retrieving of data, skilling, infrastructure and setting standards of ethics in using data.
Hyderabad: The Telangana government through its various initiatives like Telangana AI Mission, Centre of Excellence in AI, High Performance Computing Facilities and Community Centre is making all efforts to increase the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in not just governance but also among public and industry. Industries and IT Department principal secretary Jayesh Ranjan said that under the 2020 Year of AI initiative 60-plus planned programmes were carried out successfully even though the year was impacted by the pandemic. Speaking at the launch of The Artificial Intelligence Index Report 2021 by the Srini Raju Centre for IT and the Networked Economy (SRITNE) at the Indian School of Business (ISB), he highlighted that the AI framework unveiled under the IT policy focused on datasets, retrieving of data, skilling, infrastructure and setting standards of ethics in using data. “We have set up two High Performance Computing Facilities at JNTU and IIT-Hyderabad out of which the one at JNTU will be made available to researchers outside of the university as well. In addition, we have also introduced a compulsory course in AI in JNTU for students from all departments,” said Jayesh Ranjan. One of the biggest areas where the government is applying AI is in the sector of agriculture, he said and added, “about 80 tech-enabled solutions were developed by different innovators and startups in the agriculture space and we have provided these solutions to agriculture university in Telangana for their research purpose,” he informed. body_text:
The Bengaluru Police on Wednesday arrested a 25-year-old migrant worker from Bihar for allegedly uploading an AI-generated video depicting a bomb blast at Vidhana Soudha, the seat of the Karnataka legislature.
The video, posted on Instagram, showed an edited explosion at the building. The police are questioning Hazarat Ali, who uploaded it, to establish his motive and whether others were involved. They are also trying to determine whether the video was intended to cause panic or had any other purpose.
According to the police, Ali, a daily-wage pipe fitter, had come to Bengaluru a few months ago.
The incident came to light on Tuesday morning when an Instagram account named “jnx_king_h_g” uploaded the video showing the accused making a gun gesture and pretending to shoot at Vidhana Soudha, followed by an edited clip showing an explosion at the building and carrying the caption, ‘Vidhanasabha Uda Diya Bam se’.

description: AI is uncovering software vulnerabilities at an accelerating pace, leaving cybersecurity teams less time to patch flaws before hackers exploit them, experts warn.
body_text:
Advances in artificial intelligence have uncovered a stream of new software vulnerabilities that are almost certain to trigger more disruption along the lines of the outages that percolated across global government websites this week, according to seven cybersecurity professionals who spoke to Reuters.
AI helped drive a doubling of the number of digital flaws discovered year-on-year, according to research due to be published in the coming days by VulnCheck, a Massachusetts-based threat intelligence firm.
Matthew Prince, the chief executive of the digital infrastructure firm Cloudflare, told Reuters he was aware of “a bunch of additional severe vulnerabilities that are present in other pieces of critical software” and predicted busy months ⁠ahead as ​AI surfaced long-hidden weaknesses in the fabric of the internet.

title: 88% of Indian enterprises expect demand for AI-focused engineers to rise by 2030: Report
description: The new Scaler-CMR report highlights forward-deployed engineers as an emerging tech role, with India seeing a considerable rise by 2030.
body_text:
Artificial intelligence (AI) appears to be creating more job roles. About nine in 10 Indian enterprises foresee a demand for Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) increasing by 2030. At present, only one per cent of engineers work in such roles. The finding is part of a new report by AI-native technology education company Scaler and research firm CyberMedia Research (CMR).
The report is essentially a survey of about 1,000 software engineers and 200 enterprise technology decision-makers from eight metro cities and select Tier II cities. It underscores the widening gap between demand and the availability of skilled professionals.
An FDE is a tech expert who works directly with clients to customise and install software so that it aligns with their business. In essence, FDEs work at the intersection of software engineering, AI, and customer engagement. This role involves understanding the business requirements and helping companies implement AI solutions in real-world settings.

title: Microsoft AI tool outperforms doctors in complex diagnostic tests, study finds
description: A Microsoft AI system that mimics doctors’ step-by-step diagnostic process was more than twice as accurate as general physicians in solving complex medical cases, according to a study published in Science.
body_text:
Microsoft researchers say an AI tool that diagnoses patients step by step, as doctors do, was more than twice as accurate as general physicians at solving complex medical cases, according to a study published on Thursday in Science .
The model identifies and coordinates the questions that should be asked of a patient, as well as the exams and tests that should be ordered, using an “orchestrator” that organises how AI will tackle a problem by employing ⁠a ​simulated panel of clinical experts collaborating to solve diagnostic cases, according to the report.
Existing medical AI models typically take an all-at-once approach that examines all of a patient’s symptoms, lab results and imaging studies to generate a diagnosis.

description: Exposed credentials, weak access controls, and cloud misconfigurations enabled 'rogue' AI agents to hack into Indian systems, raising a bigger question: How prepared are the country's organisations for attacks that unfold at unprecedented speed and scale?
body_text:
Days after India’s nodal cybersecurity agency warned that ‘rogue’ or misaligned AI agents targeted Indian organisations and gained unauthorised access to their live systems, experts called into question enterprises’ ability to defend against such attacks where security vulnerabilities are exploited at “machine speed”.
“The lesson is not about AI tools and their tendency to go beyond their sandboxes but about our organisations failing to do their job,” Professor Sandeep Shukla, director, International Institute of Information Technology (IIIT) Hyderabad , told The Indian Express.
In an advisory dated Thursday, October 15, The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said that under-testing AI agents flouted their initial task authorisations, issued commands, invoked tools, reached the internet, and eventually gained unauthorised access to the live systems of unnamed Indian organisations.

description: It is part of World’s plans to grow the reach of its Orb-based, iris-scanning verification tech even as the online world becomes increasingly dominated by AI agents.
body_text:
World, the biometric verification startup co-founded by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, is expanding its services to partners such as Zoom and major financial firms in its latest push to drive enterprise adoption of its so-called ‘proof of human’ tools designed to keep out malicious bots.
The startup’s verification technology comes down to an orb-shaped device that captures an image of people’s irises and creates a permanent, tamper-proof record of their identity. Its broader suite of services built around this device is called World ID and looks to help organisations establish trust through these privacy-preserving, cryptographic Proofs.
World ID with Zoom will allow meeting participants to confirm that they are the same Orb-verified human connected to their account, the company said in a post on X on Sunday, October 18.

One of the options that the group has been directed to consider is a kill switch for advanced AI systems, as a mechanism of bringing them to a complete halt if they start behaving in dangerous or unexpected ways. title: AI agents cheat, can they also catch cheaters? What Google DeepMind paper says
description: Google DeepMind researchers tasked a swarm of 100 autonomous AI agents with solving mathematical conjectures and observed two key misaligned behaviours.
body_text:
What if trying to restrict how AI agents communicate could inversely make them harder to control? A new research paper by Google DeepMind suggests that autonomous multi-agent swarms may be less likely to behave in unexpected ways when operating in decentralised, self-governance environments.
The research paper titled ‘A Case Study on Emergent Cheating and Whistleblowing in Autonomous Research Swarms’ published on September 3, 2026, found that so-called ‘rogue’ AI agent swarms could use unauthorised communication channels to carry out misaligned actions. However, the same communication channels could also be used by agents to whistleblow and help detect manipulation by rogue agents.
The research findings come in the wake of the Hugging Face incident, where OpenAI-linked agents broke out of their containment, gained access to the internet, spun up message boards, communicated with each other before eventually hacking into a real-world, external platform over a span of two months.

description: Tamil Nadu’s proposed e-Sevai 2.0 platform is being designed to use artificial intelligence (AI) and integrate up to 1,000 government services, compared with the 275 available on the existing platform. The proposed system is also intended to help eligible citizens access certain services without having to submit fresh applications.
body_text: CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu’s proposed e-Sevai 2.0 platform is being designed to use artificial intelligence (AI) and integrate up to 1,000 government services, compared with the 275 available on the existing platform. The proposed system is also intended to help eligible citizens access certain services without having to submit fresh applications..The existing e-Sevai platform provides 275 services across 38 departments through 25,277 centres. It handles an average of 50,000 to 60,000 requests a day, with demand reaching 80,000 on peak days. The proposed platform is designed to accommodate an average of 60,000 to 1.2 lakh requests a day, with peak demand of up to 1.5 lakh, supporting at least 50,000 concurrent users. Named as Vetri Tamil Nadu Integrated e-Sevai 2.0 Platform,  the Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency (TNeGA) issued an Expression of Interest (EOI) inviting technology providers to propose solutions for a common platform to manage applications, approvals, documents, payments and certificates across government departments.The platform is also intended to support a “No Application” service delivery model, under which authorised government databases would be used to identify eligible beneficiaries and pre-fill application details. Where service rules permit, eligible citizens could receive services without submitting a separate application. .The platform is expected to connect around 15 departmental portals and 18 State and national digital systems. These include Aadhaar-based authentication, e-Sign, DigiLocker and payment services, as well as government databases. TNeGA estimates that around 110 terabytes of data, including databases and supporting documents from the existing e-Sevai and e-District systems, would have to be migrated.The existing e-Sevai centre network is expected to remain part of the service-delivery ecosystem. The proposed platform will have mobile applications, messaging services, call centres and IVRS, alongside other digital government platforms.A substantial part of the transition will involve migrating data from the existing e-Sevai and e-District systems including databases and supporting documents, which would have to be transferred to the new platform. .The proposed AI tools include a conversational interface in Tamil and English to help users find services, document-processing capabilities and a workbench to assist government officers in handling applications. AI is also proposed for classifying grievances, routing them to the appropriate authorities and identifying duplicate complaints. The AI system would operate within TNeGA’s environment, with citizen data not leaving that environment. The proposed platform is to run on government-provided infrastructure rather than depend on a vendor-hosted cloud service to provide seamless service.

description: From incorporating artificial intelligence and upgrading 112 emergency response systems to restructuring recruitment and workload, Karnataka has set up three high-level panels to execute a major police overhaul.
body_text:
The Karnataka government has constituted three expert committees to examine how the state police department delivers services, how it should be modernised to address emerging forms of crime and technology, and how its cadre and recruitment system should be structured to meet future requirements.
The committees, headed by retired directors-general of police (DGPs) R K Dutta, M N Reddy and Kamal Pant, have been given two months to submit their recommendations.
One committee will focus on the police-public interface and the functioning of police services, while the other panel will prepare a roadmap for modernising the department, including artificial intelligence (AI) , cyber capabilities, emergency response and the 112 system, forensic infrastructure, communications and computerisation. The third committee will examine the department’s sanctioned strength, cadre structure, recruitment rules, creation and reclassification of posts and career progression.
